w: A 60-tonne slab of Cornish granite sits in the middle of this old Hackney Marshes common, dropped in 2008 to double as sculpture and bouldering wall. The ground itself was a WWI shell factory site before becoming a 1922 recreation ground; climbers kept coming through lockdown, later documented in a 2022 photobook.
s: A 60-tonne granite boulder for climbing on old marshland
_facts: 35.5-acre common, once part of Hackney Marshes
Site of the National Projectile Factory built in 1915
60-tonne Cornish granite bouldering rock placed in the park in 2008
Subject of the 2022 photobook 'Mabley Green Class of '21'

w: Before prayers, this was the Astra Cinema, splicing martial-arts films with softcore ones until it closed in 1983. Built in 1913 as the Apollo Picture House and relaunched in 1933 as the Ambassador, it became a mosque that year, serving Stoke Newington's Turkish community with a halal butcher, school and wedding hall.
s: A 1913 cinema, later a mosque with a butcher and school
_facts: Opened 1913 as the Apollo Picture House cinema
Reopened 1933 as the Ambassador Cinema; ran as the Astra Cinema from 1974 showing martial arts and softcore films
Converted to a mosque in 1983, funded by the UK Turkish Islamic Association
Capacity 2,000; includes a halal butcher, weekend school, wedding hall and restaurant

w: Staged inside a former paint factory on Ashwin Street, the Colourworks building houses two studio theatres, rehearsal space and a cafe-bar behind its industrial brick front. Since 2007 the Green Arcola project has pushed to make it the world's first carbon-neutral theatre; Arcola Outside followed in 2021.
s: Plays and opera staged in a former paint factory
_facts: Housed in the former Colourworks paint factory on Ashwin Street, Dalston
Two studio theatres, two rehearsal studios and a cafe-bar
Green Arcola project (since 2007) aims for the world's first carbon-neutral theatre
Opened the open-air Arcola Outside in 2021
